name: fractal_dimension_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The fractal dimension (FD) of a price series measures its space-filling complexity on a scale from 1 (smooth trend) to 2 (random noise). When FD approaches 1.0, the price path is trending smoothly — ideal for trend-following. When FD approaches 1.5+, the path is noisy and random. By computing the Higuchi fractal dimension on a rolling 40-bar window and trading only when FD < 1.35 (structured, trending price action), we filter out choppy noise periods and only enter during mechanistically favorable conditions. The inefficiency exists because fractal dimension is a concept from chaos theory, not standard technical analysis, and its real-time computation on 1-min bars is uncommon outside academic research.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

exit.signal_exit: Higuchi_FD rises above 1.45 (price action becoming noisy — edge lost)

weaknesses: Higuchi FD with k_max=8 on 40 data points is at the boundary of statistical reliability — the algorithm requires k_max * N computations and smaller windows reduce accuracy significantly
FD < 1.35 filtering removes the majority of trading time — price is 'noisy' (FD > 1.35) for ~60-70% of the session, leaving a narrow window for entries
The relationship between fractal dimension and future returns is not well-established empirically on 1-min Indian equity data — the theory is from physics, not finance-specific
prior_art: Higuchi (1988) fractal dimension algorithm; Peters (1994) 'Fractal Market Analysis'; Mandelbrot's fractal geometry of markets; Ehlers references fractal concepts in his trading system books
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
